description: Empathy is great until it becomes a courtroom where you're always the defense attorney for someone else's bad behavior.
transcript: Most people don't know this or understand this, but empathy is actually one of the easiest ways to betray yourself while still feeling like a good person. My name is Mark Manson. I'm a New York Times bestselling author. And for the last 20 years, I've been teaching millions of people practical psychological tools to improve their lives. And empathy is one of the ones that most people get wrong. Because here's the thing. Once you're good at understanding people, you can justify almost anything. You can say, oh, he's avoidant, or she's overwhelmed, or they had a traumatic childhood. And suddenly, instead of setting boundaries, you're writing a psychological profile on why someone gets to treat you like shit, which honestly sounds a lot more like rationalization than empathy. Empathy is supposed to help you see people clearly, not help you ignore patterns that you don't actually want to deal with. Yes, their pain explains their behavior, but it does not excuse it. You can understand somebody deeply, but still decide that they suck and they don't get access to your life. In fact, that is kind of the whole point of empathy, because real self-respect is when your empathy stops outranking reality the reality is some people don't need more understanding they need consequences
